pr_body:
StringBuilder.Replace(string, string, ...) currently walks character-by-character to find the next location of the oldValue.  This change adds the use of MemoryExtensions.IndexOf to search for the oldValue, and only falls back to the character-by-character walk when it nears and needs to account for a chunk boundary.  It also switches to track replacement indices using more stack space and the array pool (via ValueListBuilder) rather than less stack space and array allocations.

Using the benchmark from https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/80952:

|                Method |         Toolchain |      Mean |    Error |   StdDev | Ratio | Allocated | Alloc Ratio |
|---------------------- |------------------ |----------:|---------:|---------:|------:|----------:|------------:|
| Replace_StringReplace | \main\corerun.exe |  43.71 us | 0.537 us | 0.476 us |  1.00 | 227.96 KB |        1.00 |
| Replace_StringBuilder | \main\corerun.exe | 507.24 us | 3.251 us | 2.882 us | 11.60 |  62.11 KB |        0.27 |
| Replace_StringReplace |   \pr\corerun.exe |  39.38 us | 0.440 us | 0.411 us |  0.90 | 227.96 KB |        1.00 |
| Replace_StringBuilder |   \pr\corerun.exe |  24.16 us | 0.213 us | 0.189 us |  0.55 |   58.9 KB |        0.26 |

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/80952

issue_context.title: Lacking performance of `StringBuilder.Replace`
issue_context.body:
### Description

When comparing a chain of `StringBuilder.Replace` calls to replace two or more values from a given input string, its performance is incredibly lacking. This is compared to chaining several `string.Replace` calls after one another.

### Configuration

```
BenchmarkDotNet=v0.13.3, OS=Windows 11 (10.0.22621.1105)
AMD Ryzen 5 PRO 4650U with Radeon Graphics, 1 CPU, 12 logical and 6 physical cores
.NET SDK=7.0.102
  [Host]   : .NET 6.0.13 (6.0.1322.58009), X64 RyuJIT AVX2
  .NET 6.0 : .NET 6.0.13 (6.0.1322.58009), X64 RyuJIT AVX2
  .NET 7.0 : .NET 7.0.2 (7.0.222.60605), X64 RyuJIT AVX2
```

### Data

|                Method |  Runtime |      Mean |    Error |   StdDev | Ratio | RatioSD |
|---------------------- |--------- |----------:|---------:|---------:|------:|--------:|
| Replace_StringReplace | .NET 6.0 | 184.60 us | 2.713 us | 2.265 us |  1.00 |    0.00 |
| Replace_StringBuilder | .NET 6.0 | 471.90 us | 0.821 us | 0.686 us |  2.56 |    0.03 |
|                       |          |           |          |          |       |         |
| Replace_StringReplace | .NET 7.0 |  22.07 us | 0.140 us | 0.124 us |  1.00 |    0.00 |
| Replace_StringBuilder | .NET 7.0 | 555.60 us | 0.756 us | 0.631 us | 25.17 |    0.16 |

Benchmark code: https://gist.github.com/just-ero/aefc9b5123b69c3ef49944fe6242a104.

### Regression

Seems as though `StringBuilder.Replace` used to be faster on .NET 6.0.

### Analysis

`string.Replace` does a vectorized IndexOf search.  
`StringBuilder.Replace` walks its `char` buffer and does `StartsWith` at each position.

Pretty obvious how much of a performance hit that is.
